statement: Across NYC's 42 UHF neighbourhoods, a higher share of homes with mice or rats in the building is associated with higher asthma emergency department visit rates in children aged 5-17, and the association remains after adjustment for poverty and housing problems.

graph_evidence.summary: Baltimore inner-city preschool children, mouse-sensitised and highly exposed: ED visit OR 2.1 (1.1-4.1), hospitalisation OR 36.6 (4.1-327) (Matsui et al. 2006).
150 urban children: each tenfold increase in bed mouse allergen OR 1.87 (1.21-2.88) for asthma-related health care use among mouse-sensitised children only (Torjusen et al. 2013).
School mouse allergen exposure OR 1.27 (1.05-1.54) for an asthma symptom day.
Mouse allergen reduction IRR 0.94 (0.92-0.96) for symptoms in low-income children with asthma.
Residence with rodent or insect infestation OR 2.1 (1.1-3.8) for asthma (case-control, PMID 31103883).

literature.citation: Olmedo O, Goldstein IF, Acosta L, et al. Neighborhood differences in exposure and sensitization to cockroach, mouse, dust mite, cat, and dog allergens in New York City. J Allergy Clin Immunol 2011;128(2):284-92.
literature.finding: Homes in NYC neighbourhoods with high asthma prevalence had higher mouse and cockroach allergen levels than homes in low-prevalence neighbourhoods.

prediction.magnitude: Unadjusted Spearman rho between percent of homes with mice or rats in the building (NYCHVS) and child (5-17) asthma ED rate: 0.5-0.8. Adjusted standardised coefficient (per SD of rodent share, outcome in log rate) 0.00-0.20, shrinking by more than half from the unadjusted value.
prediction.support_if: Adjusted coefficient for rodent share has a 95% CI above 0.
prediction.refute_if: Adjusted coefficient has a 95% CI below 0 (contested). A CI spanning 0 is unsettled, which is the expected verdict.

plan: Unit: UHF42 neighbourhoods. Data from the NYC Environment and Health Data Portal repository (github.com/nychealth/EHDP-data, production branch, commit recorded): measure 94 (mice or rats in the building, percent, NYCHVS), measure 634 (adults reporting mice or rats inside, CHS) as an alternative exposure, measure 1196 (asthma ED visits age 5-17, rate per 10,000) as outcome, measure 1198 (adult asthma ED rate) as a secondary outcome, measures 221 (poverty percent) and 1248 or 86 (housing problems percent) as confounders. Latest period common to all. City operational data: DOHMH Rodent Inspection (p937-wjvj) share of initial inspections with active rat signs, and 311 rodent complaints per 1,000 residents (erm2-nwe9, complaint_type 'Rodent', 2022-2024), by ZIP code mapped to UHF42, as alternative exposures. Model: OLS of log asthma ED rate on standardised exposure, poverty, housing problems; n=42, HC3 SE. Report unadjusted rho and adjusted coefficient. Figure: binned scatter and coefficient plot with the household-level research OR beside the NYC estimate.
alternatives: Poverty, housing quality, cockroach allergen, smoking and outdoor air pollution all vary with rodent infestation across neighbourhoods.
The research concerns indoor mouse allergen among sensitised children; NYC rodent measures mix rats and mice and indoor and outdoor signs.
Health care access: ED use for asthma reflects lack of primary care as well as morbidity.
n=42 gives little power to separate correlated neighbourhood measures.
